title: Change the engine oil and filter
plainEnglish: Oil is the engine’s blood. You drain the old, swap the filter, and pour in the viscosity printed on the cap — not whatever is on sale. A driveway oil change is the first real job most owners should learn.
toolsNeeded: Jack and jack stands or ramps
partsNeeded: Correct viscosity oil (cap + owner’s manual)
Oil filter that matches this engine
New crush washer if the plug uses one
safetyNotes: Never work under a car that is only on a jack. Stands or ramps, then a shake test.
Hot oil burns. Let the engine sit 10–20 minutes after a short drive.
Used oil is hazardous waste. Parts stores take it back.
steps: Read the cap and the manual for viscosity, spec, and capacity in quarts. Write the number down before you buy.
Warm the engine a few minutes so the oil flows, then shut it off and chock the wheels.
Lift the car at the factory jack points and set stands. Shake the body. If it rocks, reset.
Place the drain pan under the oil pan bolt. Crack the plug, then finish by hand so you can catch it.
Let it drain until it drips. Inspect the plug magnet or threads. Replace the crush washer if it has one.
Move the pan under the filter. Unscrew the old filter. Wipe the mount. Oil the new gasket. Hand-tighten only.
Snug the drain plug. Lower the car. Fill through the cap with a funnel, stop 0.5 qt short of capacity, wait, then read the dipstick on level ground.
Start it, watch for leaks, shut it off, recheck the stick. Reset the oil-life monitor. Write the mileage on the filter or a glove-box note.

youtube.title: How to Change Your Oil (COMPLETE Guide)
youtube.whyThisVideo: ChrisFix walks a first-timer through viscosity, the filter, jacking, and the refill — not a 90-second montage.

shopSentence: Please change the oil and filter using the viscosity and spec on the cap. I want the old filter shown and the mileage reset.
askAtTheShop: Ask which viscosity they poured and whether they used the filter SKU for this engine — not a “universal” filter.

title: Check and top off coolant the safe way
plainEnglish: Coolant keeps the engine from cooking and from freezing. The reservoir has a cold fill line. Opening a hot radiator cap is how people get scalded. Color is not a spec — the chemistry on the jug is.
partsNeeded: The exact coolant chemistry in the manual (not “universal green”)
Distilled water only if the jug is concentrate
safetyNotes: Engine cold. If the upper hose is hard or steaming, walk away.
Never mix chemistries. Dex-Cool, Asian HOAT, and European OAT are not interchangeable by color.
Coolant is toxic to pets. Wipe spills.
steps: Park level. Wait until the engine is fully cold — overnight is safest.
Find the translucent overflow tank. Read the COLD / MIN / MAX marks. Photograph them.
If it is between the marks, you are done. If it is below MIN, add the correct premix to the COLD line only.
If the tank is empty, do not guess. That is a leak or a recent job that was not burped. Do not keep driving if the gauge is climbing.
Look at the fluid: oily film, rust, or coffee-with-cream means a shop test, not another gallon of whatever is on the shelf.
Cap it until it clicks. Recheck after the next cold morning.

youtube.title: How to Check and Test Your Coolant/Antifreeze
youtube.whyThisVideo: ChrisFix shows how to test concentration and why a 50/50 mix matters before winter — not just “add green stuff.”

shopSentence: Please check the coolant level cold, tell me which chemistry is in the system, and pressure-test if it is low. Do not sell a flush unless you find rust, oil, or a failed thermostat.
askAtTheShop: Ask for the chemistry name (G-11, G-12, Dex-Cool, Honda Type 2, etc.) and a leak-down or pressure-test result — not a $180 “cooling system service” by default.

title: Map every fluid before you authorize a package
plainEnglish: Oil, trans, coolant, brake, power steering, and washer are different jobs with different intervals. A shop multi-point that wants all of them at once is a menu, not a diagnosis. Learn what each jug is for so you can say no.
timeEstimate: 30–40 minutes to watch and walk the bay
safetyNotes: Do not open a hot cooling system.
Brake fluid eats paint. Wipe immediately.
Sealed transmissions often have no dipstick — do not pry a fill plug you cannot put back.
steps: Open the manual to the maintenance schedule. Circle the fluids that are actually due by miles or time.
Under the hood, find oil cap, coolant tank, brake reservoir, washer tank. Photograph each cap.
Brake fluid should sit between MIN and MAX. If it is at MIN, pads may be worn — that is a measurement job, not a flush by default.
Transmission: if there is a dipstick, check it hot and in the gear the manual says. If there is no stick, this is a shop level-check.
Write one sentence per fluid: due / not due / unknown. That list is what you take to the counter.

youtube.title: How to Change EVERY FLUID in your Car or Truck (Oil, Transmission, Coolant, Brake, and More)
youtube.whyThisVideo: One map of the whole fluid bay so a “full service package” cannot blur oil with a trans flush.

shopSentence: I want each fluid listed separately with the spec and whether it is due. I am not authorizing a bundled flush package.
askAtTheShop: Ask them to show the maintenance schedule line they are quoting — miles or months — for each fluid.

title: Flush and bleed brake fluid
plainEnglish: Brake fluid absorbs water. After a few years it boils easier and rusts the expensive parts inside. A flush pushes new DOT 3 or DOT 4 through each corner until the old brown fluid is gone. This is not the same as topping off a low reservoir — low fluid often means worn pads.
toolsNeeded: Clear hose and bottle or one-person bleeder
Flare-nut or box wrench for bleeders
partsNeeded: 1 liter of the DOT rating on the cap (do not mix DOT 5 silicone)
Shop towels
safetyNotes: Never let the master cylinder run dry. Air in the lines is a no-brake-pedal event.
Brake fluid strips paint. Cover fenders.
If the pedal stays soft after a bleed, do not drive. Tow it.
steps: Read the cap: DOT 3 or DOT 4. Buy that. Date-stamp the bottle — old open fluid is already wet.
Suck the dirty reservoir down without scraping the bottom, then refill with new fluid.
Bleed farthest from the master first unless the manual says otherwise (often RR, LR, RF, LF).
Hose on the bleeder, crack it, pump or gravity-feed until the stream is clear and bubble-free, then snug the bleeder.
Top the reservoir every corner. Never let it hit empty.
Pump the pedal until it is hard. Hold it. If it sinks, you still have air or a leak.
Test in a parking lot at walking speed before a road.

youtube.title: How to do a Complete Brake Flush and Bleed
youtube.whyThisVideo: ChrisFix shows both the two-person pump method and a one-person bleed, plus disc and drum corners.

shopSentence: Please flush the brake fluid with the DOT rating on the cap. I want the old fluid color noted and the pedal confirmed hard before I pick the car up.
askAtTheShop: Ask which DOT they used and whether they found moisture or rust in the fluid — a flush is not a pad job.

title: Transmission drain-and-fill (not a machine flush)
plainEnglish: A drain-and-fill replaces the fluid that actually falls out of the pan — often 40–50% — plus the filter if the pan comes down. It is the conservative service. A machine flush pushes fluid through cooler lines and can move debris in a neglected box. They are not the same line item.
toolsNeeded: Funnel that fits the fill hole
partsNeeded: Exact ATF spec from the manual (WS, DW-1, Mercon LV, etc.)
Filter and pan gasket if the pan drops
New drain plug washer
safetyNotes: Confirm you can open the fill first. A seized fill plug after a drain strands the car.
Hot ATF burns. Wear gloves.
Overfill causes foaming and blown seals. Level-check the way the manual says — often hot, running, in a specific gear.
steps: Look up capacity and spec. Buy enough for a drain (often 3–5 qt) plus a little extra.
Lift and support the car. Crack the fill or dipstick path so you know you can refill.
Drain the pan or drop it. Photograph the fluid color and the magnet. Black with glitter is a conversation, not a flush.
Replace the filter if the pan is off. Clean the magnet. New gasket. Torque the pan in a star pattern.
Refill what came out, then run through the gears and level-check per the book.
Look for leaks at the pan and cooler lines after a short drive.

youtube.title: How to Change Automatic Transmission Fluid and Filter (COMPLETE Guide)
youtube.whyThisVideo: Shows the pan-drop method so you understand what a drain-and-fill actually replaces — including the filter.

shopSentence: I want a drain-and-fill with the factory ATF spec, not a machine flush. Show me the old fluid and tell me how many quarts went back in.
askAtTheShop: Ask drain-and-fill vs flush, the exact fluid spec, and whether they drop the pan for the filter.

title: Drain-and-fill vs a transmission flush
plainEnglish: A change dumps what gravity will give you. A flush exchanges nearly all of it through the cooler lines. On a healthy, regularly serviced trans, a flush can be fine. On a neglected, burnt, or mystery-history box, a flush can be the job that makes it slip. This video is the sentence you need before you initial that line.
safetyNotes: Do not authorize a flush from a code or a shudder alone. Fluid photos first.
“Lifetime fluid” still oxidizes. Time and heat count.
steps: Ask for a photo of the fluid on a paper towel: color, smell, metal.
If it is red or pink and you have service records, a flush or a change can both be valid — pick the one the maker specifies.
If it is black, burnt, or full of glitter, do not flush. Diagnose. A cheap drain may still be the first look.
Write the sentence: flush only if the fluid is in good shape and the manual allows it.
Get the line item named: drain-and-fill, pan drop plus filter, or machine flush. Those are three prices.

youtube.title: Can Changing your Transmission Fluid Cause Damage?
youtube.whyThisVideo: ChrisFix draws the change vs flush difference and when a flush can move debris in a neglected valve body.

shopSentence: Do not machine-flush this transmission unless you have inspected the fluid and the maker calls for it. I want a drain-and-fill or a diagnosis first.
askAtTheShop: Ask to see the fluid and which procedure they priced. “Transmission service” is not a procedure.

title: Replace the cabin air filter
plainEnglish: This is the filter that cleans the air you breathe. It lives behind the glove box on most cars. Shops charge $80–$120 for a 10-minute clip job. If the AC smells like a wet sock or the windshield fogs, look here first.
toolsNeeded: Optional: screwdriver or Torx for a cover
partsNeeded: Cabin filter that matches year/make/model (or the SKU on the spec sheet)
safetyNotes: Do not force the glove box past its stops — the damper arm pops off.
Wear a dust mask if the old filter is moldy.
steps: Search “[year make model] cabin filter location” or open the manual. Most drop the glove box.
Empty the glove box. Squeeze the sides past the stops or unclip the damper.
Open the plastic door. Photograph the old filter so you know which way the airflow arrow pointed.
Slide the old one out. Vacuum leaves and grit from the housing.
Install the new filter with the arrow matching the housing mark (usually toward the blower / down).
Clip the door and glove box back. Run the fan on high — it should be quieter and stronger.

youtube.title: How to PERFECTLY Maintain your First Car
youtube.whyThisVideo: The first-car video includes a real cabin-filter swap: airflow arrow, moldy old filter, and the glove-box cover. Jump to the cabin-filter chapter.

shopSentence: I will replace the cabin filter myself. If you already have it open, I only want the part at cost — not an hour of labor.
askAtTheShop: If they already charged cabin-filter labor, ask to see the old filter. An $80 labor line on a clip job is the classic pad.

title: Replace the engine air filter
plainEnglish: The engine air filter sits in a black plastic box in the engine bay. A clogged one makes the car feel tired and can trip a MAF-related code. Pop the clips, photograph the old one, drop the new one in the same orientation. Ten minutes.
toolsNeeded: Hands or a Phillips / 10 mm for box screws
partsNeeded: Engine air filter for this air box
safetyNotes: Engine off. Do not drop dirt into the open intake.
Do not oil a paper filter. Leave K&N-style cleaning to that product’s instructions.
steps: Find the air box — usually a rectangular housing with metal clips or 10 mm screws and a big rubber hose to the engine.
Unclip or unscrew the lid. Lift it just enough to slide the filter out. Do not yank the MAF sensor connector.
Photograph which way the rubber seal sat. Vacuum the box. Do not blow compressed air toward the MAF.
Set the new filter so the seal sits in the groove. Close the lid evenly. All clips on.
Start the car. No whistle at the lid means the seal seated.

youtube.title: How to PERFECTLY Maintain your First Car
youtube.whyThisVideo: Same first-car bay: he pops the engine air box, shows a filthy element, and reseals the lid. Pair with the cabin-filter chapter.

shopSentence: I can swap the engine air filter. If you quote it, I want the part price only unless the box is broken.
askAtTheShop: Ask to see the old filter. A $90 “air induction service” is not a filter.

title: Replace an in-line fuel filter (when your car still has one)
plainEnglish: Older Fords, Mazdas, and some trucks have a filter on the frame. Many modern cars hid it in the tank — there is no $18 canister to swap. If the manual has no interval, do not let a shop invent one. Fuel is flammable. Depressurize first.
toolsNeeded: Jack stands if it is under the car
partsNeeded: Correct in-line filter and new clips if they are one-time
safetyNotes: Work cold, outside, no sparks. Depressurize: pull the fuel-pump fuse and run the engine until it dies.
Have a drain pan. Residual fuel will spill.
If the filter is in the tank, this is a pump-module job — stop.
steps: Confirm the car has an accessible in-line filter. Many 2005+ cars do not.
Relieve rail pressure. Disconnect the battery if you will be near metal tools and fuel.
Photograph hose orientation. Arrow on the new filter points toward the engine.
Release the quick-connects or flare nuts. Swap the filter. Click the lines fully home.
Reinstall the fuse. Key on to prime. Check for leaks before you start.

youtube.title: How To Replace a Ford Fuel Filter (homemade disconnect tool)
youtube.whyThisVideo: ChrisFix shows Ford-style quick-disconnects — the usual backyard filter — and a pen-cap trick if you do not have the tool.

shopSentence: Does this VIN have a serviceable in-line fuel filter? If it is in the tank, I do not want a made-up canister line.
askAtTheShop: Ask where the filter lives on this VIN. “Fuel system service” is not a location.

title: Replace brake pads and rotors
plainEnglish: Pads are the sacrificial blocks. Rotors are the discs they squeeze. When pads hit the wear tab you hear a squeal. When they are gone you hear grinding — that is metal cutting the rotor. A complete job is pads, hardware, greased pins, and rotors measured against the discard thickness stamped on the hat.
partsNeeded: Pads and hardware kit
Rotors if below discard or deeply grooved
Silicone paste for guide pins (not petroleum grease)
Blue Loctite if the bracket bolts used it
safetyNotes: Never rely on the jack alone.
Do not press the pedal with a caliper hanging.
Pump the pedal after assembly until it is hard — before you move the car.
Brake dust: wet-clean, do not blow.
steps: Loosen lugs on the ground. Lift and stand the corner. Remove the wheel.
Unbolt the caliper, hang it from a wire — do not stretch the hose.
Photograph pad orientation and hardware. Remove the bracket if the rotor is trapped.
Measure rotor thickness vs the stamped minimum. If it is under, replace. Do not machine a rotor that is already at spec.
Clean the hub face so the new rotor sits flat. One lug nut holds it while you work.
Compress the piston slowly with the reservoir cap off. Watch the fluid level so it does not overflow.
Grease only the contact ears and guide pins with the right grease. Pads in. Bracket torque. Caliper torque.
Wheels on, star-pattern torque to the door-jamb or manual number. Pump the pedal. Bed the pads per the pad maker.

youtube.title: How to Replace Brake Pads and Rotors (COMPLETE Guide)
youtube.whyThisVideo: The complete pad-and-rotor job: pins, grease, Loctite, torque, and the mandatory pedal-pump at the end.

shopSentence: Measure inner and outer pad thickness in millimeters on both sides of that axle, and rotor thickness vs the discard spec. I will not authorize rotors without a number.
askAtTheShop: Ask for millimeters, not “they’re due.” If rotors are above discard, machining or reuse can be valid.

title: Bleed brakes by yourself with a $5 bottle
plainEnglish: A second person pumping the pedal is the classic bleed. If you are alone, a bottle of fluid and a clear hose that stays submerged keeps air from getting sucked back in. Still: never let the reservoir go empty.
timeEstimate: 30 minutes to build + 45 minutes to bleed
partsNeeded: Fresh DOT 3 or DOT 4 matching the cap
safetyNotes: If the pedal is soft after, do not drive.
Keep the hose end under fluid so air cannot reverse.
steps: Drill the bottle cap for a snug hose and a tiny vent hole.
Fill the bottle so the hose end stays submerged. Clip the other end on the bleeder.
Crack the bleeder. Pump slowly. Watch bubbles. Keep the master topped up.
When the stream is clear, close the bleeder before you pull the hose.
Repeat corners in the book order. Confirm a hard pedal.

youtube.title: How to Make a One Person Brake Bleeder for Under $5
youtube.whyThisVideo: Builds the one-person check-valve bottle so a solo owner can finish a flush without a helper.

shopSentence: Please bleed the brakes until the pedal is hard. I do not need a full flush unless the fluid is dark or old.
askAtTheShop: Ask whether they are bleeding after a pad job or selling a flush. Those are different.

title: Check and adjust the parking brake
plainEnglish: The parking brake is a cable (or an electric motor) that locks the rear brakes so the car does not roll. If the handle climbs to the sky or the car rolls on a driveway, the cable is slack or the little shoes inside a rear disc hat are worn. Adjustment is model-specific. If you have an electronic EPB, do not yank the cable — you need a scan-tool retract.
toolsNeeded: Wrench for the cable adjuster (often under the console)
Jack stands if you adjust shoes
partsNeeded: Cable or rear shoes only if they are worn through
safetyNotes: Chock the front wheels.
Electronic parking brakes need a service mode. Forcing the caliper wrecks the motor.
A dragging cable cooks the rear brakes.
steps: Count the clicks to full engagement. Compare to the manual (often 5–8).
On a slight grade, set the brake and see if the car holds in neutral. If it rolls, it is not adjusted.
Look up whether this car is cable, drum-in-hat, or electric. Electric: stop and use the shop sentence.
Cable: find the adjuster under the console or at the equalizer. Tighten a few turns, then retest. Do not over-tighten — the rears will drag.
If the cable is already tight and it still will not hold, the rear shoes or the electric actuator need a tech.

youtube.title: How to adjust a parking brake cable
youtube.whyThisVideo: No single well-known video covers cable, drum-in-hat, and electronic EPB. Use the search — then match your handle type.

shopSentence: The parking brake does not hold on a grade. Please tell me if this is a cable adjustment, rear shoe service, or an electronic parking-brake retract.
askAtTheShop: Ask which system you have and whether they put the EPB in service mode before compressing a rear caliper.

title: Bleed after a pad job if the pedal is soft
plainEnglish: You do not always flush after pads — but if you opened a line, or the pedal is soft, you bleed. Soft pedal after pads is usually a piston that was not seated or air. Do not drive it “to see if it firms up.”
partsNeeded: DOT fluid matching the cap
safetyNotes: Hard pedal in the driveway before the street.
steps: After pads, pump the pedal with the car still on stands until it firms.
If it stays soft, bleed the corners you worked, then the rest if needed.
Keep the reservoir full. Close bleeders tight, not stripped.
Road-test from a crawl. Then a slightly harder stop in an empty lot.

youtube.title: How to do a Complete Brake Flush and Bleed
youtube.whyThisVideo: Same bleed video — use it after a pad job when the pedal is not honest yet.

shopSentence: The pedal is soft after the pad job. Please bleed and confirm a hard pedal before I take the car.
askAtTheShop: Ask whether a hose was opened. Soft pedal after pads is their problem to finish, not yours to “break in.”

title: Set tire pressure from the door-jamb sticker
plainEnglish: The number on the tire sidewall is a maximum, not your fill target. Your car’s cold PSI is on the driver’s door sticker. Low tires wear the edges, waste fuel, and light the TPMS horseshoe. Check them cold — before you drive.
partsNeeded: Valve caps if they are missing
safetyNotes: Do not fill to the sidewall max.
If a tire is more than about 8 PSI low, look for a nail before you just air it up every week.
steps: Read the door-jamb placard: front PSI, rear PSI, spare PSI. Photograph it.
Check cold. Unscrew the cap. Press the gauge straight on until the hiss stops.
Add air in short bursts. Recheck. Let some out with the gauge stem if you overshot.
Do all four, then the spare if you have a real one. Caps back on.
If the TPMS light stays on, drive a few minutes above 20 mph, or use the reset in the manual.

youtube.title: How to Properly Check and Fill Tires on Your Car
youtube.channel: 1A Auto: Repair Tips & Secrets Only Mechanics Know
youtube.whyThisVideo: 1A Auto shows door-sticker vs sidewall max, a cold check, and why TPMS is not a substitute for a gauge.

shopSentence: Please set all four tires and the spare to the door-jamb cold PSI, not the sidewall max. I want the numbers written on the RO.
askAtTheShop: Ask them to write the PSI they set. “We aired them up” is not a number.

title: Rotate the tires
plainEnglish: Front tires wear differently than rears. Rotation moves them so a set lasts longer. Directional tires (arrow on the sidewall) can only swap front-to-back on the same side. After a rotation, reset TPMS if the car needs a relearn, and torque the lugs in a star.
toolsNeeded: Jack and four jack stands or a two-post lift
safetyNotes: Never leave a car on a jack to swap four corners. Stands under factory points.
Torque on the ground, star pattern.
Do not rotate a space-saver spare into the set.
steps: Read the manual for the pattern: forward-cross, rearward-cross, or side-to-side for directional.
Loosen all lugs on the ground. Lift and support so all four wheels can come off, or do one axle at a time if you understand the pattern.
Move each wheel to its new corner. Directional arrows must still point forward.
Hand-start lugs. Lower. Torque to the spec (often 80–100 lb-ft) in a star.
Set PSI per the door sticker — fronts and rears may differ. Recalibrate TPMS if the car asks.

youtube.title: How to rotate tires pattern jack stands
youtube.whyThisVideo: Rotation patterns differ by drive type and directional tread. Use the search plus your manual — we will not invent a one-car ID.

shopSentence: Please rotate on the factory pattern, torque the lugs to spec, and set door-jamb PSI. Recalibrate TPMS if this car needs it.
askAtTheShop: Ask which pattern they used and the lug torque. A rotation should not require new TPMS sensors unless one already failed.

title: Change a flat and use the spare
plainEnglish: A flat on the shoulder is a roadside job, not a personality test. You loosen the lugs on the ground, lift at the factory point, swap the spare, and torque when it is down. The donut is a get-home tire — 50 mph, short distance, then a real tire.
toolsNeeded: The jack and lug wrench that came with the car
Owner’s manual for the jack point
partsNeeded: Inflated spare (check it tonight, not on the highway)
safetyNotes: Hazards on. Far from traffic. People stand in front of the guardrail, not in the lane.
Never crawl under a car on the scissor jack.
Do not use the scissor jack on a slope or soft shoulder if you can avoid it.
steps: Hazards, park, wheel chock opposite the flat. Get everyone out of the car, away from traffic.
Dig out the spare, jack, and wrench. Find the jack point in the manual — a notch in the pinch weld, not the floor pan.
Crack the lugs loose while the tire still has weight on it.
Jack until the tire clears. Remove lugs, swap the spare, hand-thread lugs.
Lower. Torque in a star as best you can with the factory wrench, then to a shop torque wrench that day.
The donut is temporary. Repair or replace the flat. Reset TPMS when the real tire is back.

youtube.title: How to Change a Tire (plus jacking it up)
youtube.whyThisVideo: ChrisFix treats jacking and the wheel swap as one skill: chocks, points, stands vs roadside jack, star pattern.

shopSentence: I have a donut on. Please mount and balance a proper tire, torque the lugs, and set door-jamb PSI.
askAtTheShop: Ask whether the flat is repairable (nail in the tread center) or needs a new tire. Plugs from the outside are not a shop repair.

title: Understand and reset a TPMS light
plainEnglish: A solid horseshoe means a tire is low. A flashing horseshoe usually means a dead sensor battery or a failed relearn after a rotation. Air the tires to the door sticker first. Then drive. Only then chase sensors.
toolsNeeded: Owner’s manual for the reset button or menu
safetyNotes: A flashing light is not “just reset it” if a tire is actually flat.
Sensor batteries last about 7–10 years. They die with the sensor, not as a $5 coin cell you pop out.
steps: Solid light: gauge all four plus spare. Fill to the placard. Caps on.
Drive 2+ minutes above about 20 mph. Many systems clear themselves.
If the manual has a TPMS reset or Honda-style calibration, do that after the pressures are right.
Flashing light after correct PSI: the system is sick. That is a sensor or module, not more air.
After a rotation, some cars need a relearn tool. That is a $20–$40 shop line, not four new sensors by default.

youtube.title: How to Reset Low Tire Pressure Light (TPMS)
youtube.whyThisVideo: ChrisFix shows the door sticker, why all four tires were low after a temperature drop, and the drive-to-clear step.

shopSentence: The TPMS light is on. I set door-jamb PSI. If it still flashes, please tell me which sensor failed — do not quote four sensors first.
askAtTheShop: Ask solid vs flashing, and which corner IDs as bad. Four sensors is a last step.

title: What a proper tire repair looks like
plainEnglish: A string plug from the outside is a get-home hack. A proper repair is from the inside: injury removed, patch-plug through the tread center. Shoulder and sidewall punctures are scrap. This is the film you want if a shop says they “fixed” a tire.
safetyNotes: Do not repair a puncture outside the tread center.
Do not drive on a tire that was run flat enough to break the sidewall.
steps: Ask where the injury is. Center tread: maybe repairable. Shoulder or sidewall: replace.
Ask them to dismount the tire and patch from the inside. A plug-only from outside is not the industry repair.
If they used sealant or a string plug, treat it as temporary. Get a real repair or a new tire.
After a proper repair, rebalance and set PSI.

youtube.title: Tire Safety Starts with Proper Tire Repair
youtube.whyThisVideo: The Tire Industry Association shows why an inside repair matters and how a bad plug can separate a belt.

shopSentence: If this puncture is in the center tread, I want an industry inside repair, not a string plug. If it is in the sidewall, replace the tire.
askAtTheShop: Ask them to show the injury on the inside of the tire. No photo, no authorization.

title: Jump-start a dead 12-volt battery
plainEnglish: A dead battery is usually lights left on or an old battery — not a dead engine. Cable order matters so you do not spark on the battery. Last clamp goes to bare metal on the dead car, not the dead negative post.
toolsNeeded: Jumper cables (thick, long) or a pack-style jump box
Owner’s manual for jump points on cars with a trunk battery
safetyNotes: Do not jump a cracked or frozen battery.
Keep cables off belts and fans.
Hybrids and EVs: use the designated 12V jump posts only. Never touch the orange high-voltage cables.
steps: Both cars in park, parking brakes, accessories off. Confirm the dead battery is 12V lead-acid or AGM, not a damaged case.
Red on dead positive. Red on good positive. Black on good negative. Black on unpainted metal on the dead car (strut tower bolt), away from the battery.
Start the good car. Wait a minute. Start the dead car.
Remove in reverse: black off ground, black off good negative, reds off.
Drive 20+ minutes or charge it. If it dies again overnight, test the battery and the alternator — do not keep jumping.

youtube.title: How to Properly Jump Start a Car
youtube.whyThisVideo: ChrisFix is obsessive about the last ground clamp — that is the step most owners get wrong.

shopSentence: It needed a jump. Please load-test the battery and check charging voltage at 2,000 RPM before quoting an alternator.
askAtTheShop: Ask for resting volts, cranking volts, and running volts. Those three numbers separate battery from alternator.

title: Test the 12-volt battery with a $20 meter
plainEnglish: A healthy rested battery reads about 12.6 volts. While cranking it should not crash below about 10 volts. That $20 multimeter is the difference between buying a battery and buying an alternator you did not need.
toolsNeeded: Digital multimeter set to DC volts
safetyNotes: Do not short the probes across both posts.
Corroded terminals lie. Clean them first.
steps: Engine off, lights off, car sat at least 30 minutes if you can.
Meter on 20V DC. Red on +, black on −. Read: about 12.6 full, about 12.2 hungry, under about 12.0 needs charge and a retest.
Have a helper crank. Watch the lowest number. A plunge under about 10 V while cranking is a weak battery.
If it starts, go to the alternator test (running 13.8–14.7 V).
A parts-store load test is fine — take the printout, do not take their upsell as gospel.

youtube.title: How to Test a Car Battery with a Multimeter
youtube.whyThisVideo: Six minutes: resting voltage and a cranking load with a cheap meter.

shopSentence: Please print a battery load test and the charging voltage. I do not want an alternator unless the running voltage is out of range.
askAtTheShop: Ask for the CCA result and the voltage printout. “It's bad” is not a test.

title: Replace a 12-volt battery
plainEnglish: Negative cable off first, then positive, then the hold-down. The new battery must match group size and CCA, not just “it fits in the tray.” Positive on first, negative last. Many radios will want a code. Recycle the old one — the core is worth money.
toolsNeeded: Memory saver is optional — most cars relearn idle
partsNeeded: Correct group size and CCA
Hold-down hardware if the old one is rusted
safetyNotes: Negative first off, last on.
Do not lay tools across both posts.
Some cars hide the battery under a seat or in the trunk — use those jump posts, not guesses.
steps: Confirm group size (often on the old label) and CCA vs the manual.
Engine off. Negative cable off. Then positive. Then the hold-down clamp.
Lift straight up. Batteries are heavy. Set it on cardboard, not painted fenders.
Clean the tray and cable ends. Set the new battery so + and − match the cables.
Hold-down on. Positive on. Negative on. Start it. Return the old battery for the core.

youtube.title: How to Test and Replace a Bad Car Battery (COMPLETE Ultimate Guide)
youtube.whyThisVideo: ChrisFix tests first, then replaces — so you do not throw a good battery at a bad alternator.

shopSentence: I want a battery that matches the OEM group size and CCA. Keep the core credit on the RO.
askAtTheShop: Ask group size, CCA, and warranty months. “Top of the line” is not a spec.

title: Test the alternator before you buy one
plainEnglish: The alternator is the engine-driven charger. Engine running, you should see roughly 13.8–14.7 volts at the battery. If headlights dim and voltage sits at 12.2 while running, the alternator (or a cable) is the suspect — after you proved the battery.
safetyNotes: Keep hands off belts and fans.
A failing alternator can spike voltage and cook modules — do not ignore a battery light.
steps: Confirm the battery is charged enough to start (about 12.4+).
Start the engine. Meter on the battery: 13.8–14.7 V is the usual healthy window.
Turn on headlights, blower, rear defrost. Voltage should stay above about 13.2. A collapse toward 12 V is a weak alternator or a bad ground.
Over 15 V is also bad — a failed regulator. Stop driving if you can.
Squeal from the pulley is a belt or bearing, not a software update.

youtube.title: How to Test an Alternator
youtube.whyThisVideo: ChrisFix puts a load on the charging system and shows the voltage window a $20 meter can prove.

shopSentence: Please measure charging voltage at idle and at 2,000 RPM with loads on. I will not authorize an alternator from the battery light alone.
askAtTheShop: Ask for the running voltage number. A battery light can be a belt, a ground, or the regulator.

title: Read a check-engine code with a cheap scanner
plainEnglish: The light is a pointer, not a parts list. A $20–$80 OBD-II dongle plugs under the dash, usually above the driver’s left shin. You read P0xxx, write it down, then translate it — you do not clear it and hope. AutoShield’s /obd desk will read the same code you typed.
toolsNeeded: Any ELM327 / generic OBD-II scanner or a Bluetooth dongle + phone app
safetyNotes: Key on, engine as the tool asks. Do not clear codes before you write them down — freeze-frame data disappears.
We do not sell a dongle. A $20 tool is enough to read a generic code.
steps: Find the 16-pin port under the dash, driver’s side. Plug in. Key to RUN.
Read codes. Write the exact code (P0420, P0301). Photograph the screen.
Read freeze-frame if the tool has it: RPM, temp, speed when it set.
Do not clear yet. Look the code up — here at /obd or in a repair article. A code is a test plan.
Clear only after a repair, then drive to see if it returns.

youtube.title: BlueDriver OBD2 Diagnostic Scan Tool Review (reads ABS, Airbag, Tranny Codes)
youtube.whyThisVideo: ChrisFix shows where the port is and what a phone dongle actually reads — including why a $20 tool still beats guessing.

shopSentence: I pulled this code on a cheap scanner: [code]. Please diagnose that code — do not quote a catalytic converter or a coil pack from the number alone.
askAtTheShop: Ask for the factory code title and the test they will run. P0420 is not automatically a converter.

title: Scan the car the way you would a first car
plainEnglish: Before you buy pads or ignore a light, plug in and read everything the cheap tool can see. A first-car walkthrough shows the port, the app, and how a check-engine light can be a bulb — or something that needs a real test.
toolsNeeded: Bluetooth OBD-II dongle or a handheld $20 reader
safetyNotes: Write codes down before you clear.
ABS and airbag lights are not “check engine.” A basic dongle may not read them.
steps: Plug in under the dash. Pair the app. Run a full scan if the tool offers it.
Separate engine codes from body codes (lights, camera). They are different jobs.
Photograph the list. Bring it to /obd and to the shop.
Do not reset monitors the day before an emissions test unless you know what you are doing.

youtube.title: How to PERFECTLY Maintain your First Car
youtube.whyThisVideo: The OBD chapter is filmed like a first owner: port location, whole-system scan, then he actually chases the codes.

shopSentence: Here is the scan printout. Please price diagnosis for these codes, not a parts cannon.
askAtTheShop: Ask which code they will test first and what passing looks like.

title: Replace a headlight bulb
plainEnglish: A dark headlight is usually a bulb, not a whole lamp. Access is from the engine bay or a fender liner. Do not touch halogen glass with bare fingers — oil makes a hot spot and the new bulb dies early. Sealed LED assemblies are a different, expensive job.
toolsNeeded: Possible 10 mm for a housing shift
partsNeeded: Correct bulb number from the manual (H11, 9005, etc.) — buy a pair
safetyNotes: Halogen glass: gloves only.
HID/xenon systems can hold high voltage. If it is not a simple halogen plug, stop.
Aim the lights after if you removed the housing.
steps: Confirm halogen vs HID vs LED in the manual. LED modules are usually not a $12 bulb.
Open the hood. Find the dust cap behind the lamp. Unplug the connector — rock it, do not yank wires.
Release the spring clip or twist collar. Pull the old bulb. Compare the new one in the box for damage.
Install without touching the glass. Seat the tabs. Dust cap on. Connector clicked.
Lights on. Have a helper confirm both sides. Replace in pairs so the colors match.

youtube.title: How to Replace a Headlight Bulb (Tips and Tricks)
youtube.whyThisVideo: Tips that apply across cars: do not touch the glass, check the box, and this is not a model-specific teardown.

shopSentence: I need the halogen bulb replaced, both sides, part number from the manual. If this is a sealed LED, quote the assembly separately.
askAtTheShop: Ask halogen vs LED before you approve $400. A bulb is not a housing.

title: Fix a blinker that is dark or hyper-flashing
plainEnglish: A turn signal that blinks twice as fast usually means that corner’s bulb is out — the flasher is telling on you. Rear access is often through the trunk liner. LED upgrades without a resistor hyper-flash on purpose. Match the bulb number stamped on the old glass.
toolsNeeded: Screwdriver or 8–10 mm for the housing
partsNeeded: Correct bulb (3157, 7443, 7507, etc.)
safetyNotes: Let the lamp cool.
If the socket is melted, stop — that is a housing or ground, not another bulb.
steps: Hazard lights on. Walk around. Note which corner is dark or dim.
Open the trunk or hood. Remove the access cover or the two nuts holding the lamp.
Twist the socket, pull the bulb, compare the number on the metal base.
New bulb in, seated, twist lock. Test before you button the liner.
If it still hyper-flashes with a good bulb, look at the ground and the opposite side. If you installed LEDs, you need the load the car expects.

youtube.title: How to replace turn signal bulb car trunk access
youtube.whyThisVideo: Blinker access is model-specific. Search your year/make/model plus “turn signal bulb” — we will not invent a Civic-only ID as if it were universal.

shopSentence: The [left rear] turn signal is out or hyper-flashing. Please replace the bulb and check the socket. I do not want a new lamp unless the socket is melted.
askAtTheShop: Ask bulb vs housing. Hyper-flash after an LED upgrade is a load issue, not a failed module by default.

title: Replace windshield wiper blades
plainEnglish: Streaks in the rain are a $20 part, not a $70 wiper service. Most arms are a J-hook: lift, press the tab, slide off, click the new one on. Measure the old blades — driver and passenger are often different lengths. Do not let the bare arm smack the glass.
toolsNeeded: Towel to rest the arm if you need both hands
partsNeeded: Blades in the correct lengths (check a parts-store lookup or the old blade stamp)
safetyNotes: Hold the arm when the blade comes off. It will spring into the glass.
Winter: do not rip a blade frozen to the windshield.
steps: Look up sizes or measure the old rubber. Buy the pair plus the rear if you have one.
Lift the arm. Press the lock tab. Slide the old blade off the hook.
Slide the new blade on until it clicks. Tug it. Lower gently onto the glass.
Repeat the other side. Spray washer fluid and wipe on low. No chatter, no streaks.

youtube.title: How to Replace Windshield Wipers on Your Car (Easy)
youtube.whyThisVideo: Two-minute J-hook lesson — the connector on most cars. Learn it in daylight, not in a storm.

shopSentence: I will install the blades. If you already have them on the RO, I want parts only.
askAtTheShop: Ask beam vs frame and the two lengths. Labor on wipers is almost always padding.

title: Fill washer fluid and stop the streaky smear
plainEnglish: The blue jug under the hood is washer fluid, not coolant. In winter you want a mix that will not freeze in the lines. If the pump clicks and nothing hits the glass, the tank is empty, the hose is off, or the nozzle is clogged — not a new pump by default.
partsNeeded: Washer fluid rated for your climate
safetyNotes: Do not pour coolant into the washer tank. The caps are different on purpose.
Do not use household detergent — it eats the pump.
steps: Find the tank with the windshield icon. Open it.
Fill with washer fluid. In freeze country, use −20 °F fluid, not leftover summer mix.
Spray. If it dribbles, poke the nozzle with a pin. If it is silent, check the fuse before a pump.
Replace blades if the glass still smears after a full tank.

youtube.title: How to Replace Windshield Wipers on Your Car (Easy)
youtube.whyThisVideo: Wipers and washers are one visibility job. After you fill the tank, the ChrisFix blade swap is the other half.

shopSentence: Washer spray is weak. Please check fluid, hose, and nozzles before quoting a pump.
askAtTheShop: Ask them to show the hose on the tank. A $180 pump is last.

title: Replace spark plugs when the job is actually DIY
plainEnglish: Plugs ignite the mix. On a four-cylinder with coils on top, this can be a driveway job. On a V6 where the back bank is under the cowl or the intake, it is a shop job. One coil at a time so you do not mix the wires. Hand-thread so you do not cross-thread a $1,200 head.
timeEstimate: 1–3 hours if they are on top
toolsNeeded: Torque wrench in inch-pounds if the book uses it
partsNeeded: The exact plug (iridium vs copper) and the gap the manual lists
safetyNotes: Engine cold. A hot aluminum head is easy to strip.
If a plug is in a deep well, blow the dirt out before it falls in.
Do not use anti-seize unless the plug maker says so — many modern plugs are coated and torque will be wrong.
steps: Confirm access. If you cannot see the back plugs without removing an intake, pay the shop.
Pull one coil or wire. Blow the well clean. Unscrew the plug. Compare the color to a chart — oil or coolant on the porcelain is a bigger problem.
Gap the new plug if the book says to. Hand-thread until it seats, then torque to spec.
A dab of dielectric grease in the boot. Coil back on. Next cylinder. Never leave two coils off at once if you can avoid it.
Start it. If it misfires, you swapped a connector or did not seat a coil.

youtube.title: Spark Plug Replacement DIY (the ULTIMATE Guide)
youtube.whyThisVideo: ChrisFix covers gap, dielectric grease, anti-seize debate, and how to get a plug out without wrecking the well.

shopSentence: If the rear bank needs the intake off, I want that labor explained. If the plugs are on top, I may DIY — quote parts only.
askAtTheShop: Ask whether all plugs are accessible from above. A “tune-up package” is not a diagnosis for a single-cylinder misfire.

title: Swap a coil only after the misfire follows it
plainEnglish: A coil is the puck on top of each plug on most modern engines. A P0301 (cylinder 1 misfire) is not a four-pack of coils. Swap the #1 coil with another hole. If the code follows the coil, you found the part. If it stays on hole 1, look at the plug, injector, or compression.
toolsNeeded: Scan tool to read which cylinder
partsNeeded: One coil of the correct type — not a set unless the swap test says so
safetyNotes: Engine off, key out.
Do not pry on the boot like a crowbar — twist and pull straight up.
steps: Read the code. P0302 means cylinder 2, not “needs a tune-up.”
Unplug and unbolt that coil. Swap it with a neighbor. Clear the code. Drive.
If the misfire moves, replace that coil. If it stays, replace the plug next, then stop guessing.
Dielectric grease in the new boot. Bolt snug, connector clicked.

youtube.title: How to Change Ignition Coil
youtube.whyThisVideo: AutoZone’s how-to shows the connector, the single bolt, and seating the new coil on the plug — the motion you copy after the swap test.

shopSentence: Please do the coil swap test on the misfiring cylinder before quoting a set of coils.
askAtTheShop: Ask which cylinder and whether the code followed the coil. A four-pack is not a test.

title: Jack the car on the right points — then use stands
plainEnglish: The jack lifts. The stands hold. The pinch weld or the frame pad in the manual is the only place that is supposed to take that load. A jack on the oil pan, the floor stampings, or the plastic skirt will fold the car. Shake the body before you put a single body part under it.
timeEstimate: 15 minutes to learn, every time you lift
toolsNeeded: Floor jack rated for the vehicle weight
partsNeeded: Hockey puck or pinch-weld pad if the manual allows it
safetyNotes: Level, solid ground. Asphalt in July can swallow a stand.
Parking brake on. Chock the end that stays down.
Never a bumper, never a control arm unless the book says so.
If it fails the shake test, reset. Pride is cheaper than a hospital.
steps: Read the jack-point diagram. On unibody cars it is usually a reinforced pinch-weld notch.
Chock. Loosen lugs if the wheel is coming off.
Center the jack pad on the point. Lift slowly. Watch the pad — if it walks, lower and reset.
Set the stand under the adjacent factory support point. Lower the car onto the stand. Jack stays as a backup, not the only support.
Shake the car hard. If a stand ticks or walks, start over.
To lower: jack the car off the stand, remove the stand, then lower slowly.

youtube.title: How to Change a Tire (plus jacking it up)
youtube.whyThisVideo: The tire video is the jacking lesson most owners actually need: points, chocks, and why a scissor jack is a spare-tire tool, not a work stand.

shopSentence: I need the car on a lift for [job]. I will not authorize work done on a floor jack in the parking lot.
askAtTheShop: If you DIY, ask a parts counter to confirm stand rating vs curb weight. Cheap stands fail at the pawl.

title: Put the whole car on four stands
plainEnglish: A rotation or a full brake job wants all four wheels off. You lift one end, set two stands, then the other end — never a steep angle that tips a stand. This is the extra video when the spare-tire jack is not enough.
safetyNotes: Raise in stages so the car stays level.
Do not yank on a wheel while the car is only on a jack.
steps: Chock. Lift the front at the factory point. Set two stands at the front support points. Lower onto them.
Move to the rear. Repeat. Keep stand heights even.
Shake. If a stand walks, reset that corner.
Leave the jack as a third point under a factory pad if you have room.

youtube.title: How To SAFELY Lift Your Car On Jack Stands
youtube.whyThisVideo: A dedicated stand-and-level walkthrough — verified ID — for when you need four corners, not just a spare.

shopSentence: If this job needs four wheels off, I want it on a lift, not four cheap stands in the lot.
askAtTheShop: Ask whether they use a lift. Parking-lot “mobile tech” on a bottle jack is a no.

title: Walk a used car before you fall in love
plainEnglish: A for-sale car is a story. You want panel gaps, tire dates, cold-start exhaust, and the underside — rust, leaks, crumpled frame rails. Film it. If the seller will not let you, that is the answer.
safetyNotes: Do not crawl under a car on the seller’s rickety jack.
Meet in daylight. Bring a licensed driver if you are not buying yet.
steps: Paper first: title in the seller’s name, asking price in writing, service records.
Walk the body in sun: mismatched paint, overspray, inconsistent gaps.
Tires: brand match, tread even, DOT date code (older than 6 years is a talking point).
Cold start: watch the tailpipe. Blue or sweet white that does not clear is a walk-away.
Underside: wet oil, crushed rails, wet strut towers. Interior: wet carpets (flood).
Scan before they start it if you can. Write every code.
Then a PPI — a paid independent inspection. This walk is not a PPI.

youtube.title: How to Inspect a Used Car for Purchase
youtube.whyThisVideo: ChrisFix’s roadside checklist: sign, body, interior, underside — the order a non-mechanic can film.

shopSentence: I want a pre-purchase inspection: compression or power balance, leaks, frame, and a scan of all modules. Written notes, not a thumbs-up.
askAtTheShop: Ask the inspector to film the lift. If a dealer refuses an independent PPI, walk.

title: What to film for a pre-purchase inspection
plainEnglish: A PPI is a paid hour on a lift, not a Carfax. You film title, VIN plate, cold start, test drive, and the inspector’s pointer on the lift. A checklist keeps you from skipping paperwork. Regular Car Reviews is for the culture of the price — not the torque spec.
safetyNotes: Do not skip a lift inspection on a 10-year-old car to “save” $150.
Flood, salvage, and odometer stories live in the title — read it.
steps: Film the VIN on the dash, the door sticker, and the title. They must match.
Film a cold start from the tailpipe and the dash (no warning lights hidden by a start).
Film the test drive: brake pull, shudder, trans flare, wheel bearing drone.
At the shop, film the lift: rust, leaks, tires, pad thickness if they show it.
Keep the written report. That paper is your negotiation, not a vibe.

youtube.title: Buying a Used Car Checklist: How to Inspect for Red Flags
youtube.whyThisVideo: A structured checklist: paperwork, exterior, interior, drivetrain, test drive — the chapters to film.

shopSentence: Please do a PPI with a written report: leaks, frame, codes, and wear items with measurements.
askAtTheShop: Ask what they will not certify. A PPI is an opinion with photos, not a warranty.

title: The advertised price is not the out-the-door price
plainEnglish: Dealerships advertise a number that is not what you pay. Fees, add-ons, and “already applied” credits show up in the box. Regular Car Reviews is context for that conversation — not a how-to torque video. Walk if the out-the-door number cannot be written in one line.
safetyNotes: Do not sign a blank “we will figure fees later.”
Add-ons (ceramic, nitrogen, VIN etch) are optional until you initial them.
steps: Screenshot the advertised price and the VIN.
Ask for out-the-door: tax, title, doc, add-ons. One number.
Cross out every add-on you did not request.
If the number moves after you sit down, leave. There is another car.

youtube.title: The Car Price You Saw Online Was Never Real (The Roman Report)
youtube.whyThisVideo: Roman on advertised vs real price — the culture of the desk, so you know what “out the door” is supposed to mean.

shopSentence: Write the out-the-door price including tax, title, and fees. I will not initial protection packages I did not ask for.
askAtTheShop: Ask them to print the buyer’s order before you talk monthly payment. Payment is how fees hide.

title: What not to say at the service writer’s window
plainEnglish: You are not there to perform competence. You are there to describe the symptom, hand over the code, and ask for a test. “Just do whatever it needs” is how a $90 diagnosis becomes a $2,400 menu. Scotty is blunt. Use the sentences, skip the swagger.
toolsNeeded: Written symptom + code + when it happens
safetyNotes: Do not lie about what you already tried.
Do not authorize work you cannot repeat back in one sentence.
steps: Write: noise / light / leak, when it happens, and the code if you have one.
Do not diagnose for them (“it's the catalytic converter”). Describe.
Ask for the test and the pass/fail. Then the price.
If the list is long, ask what is unsafe this week vs what can wait.
Take the old parts or a photo. That is not rude.

youtube.title: Never Say This to a Mechanic
youtube.whyThisVideo: Scotty’s five things you should not say — including why a cheap scan printout changes the conversation.

shopSentence: Here is the symptom and the code. Please diagnose that. I will authorize the test, then the repair after I hear the result.
askAtTheShop: Ask them to separate diagnosis hours from repair hours on the RO.

title: Read a repair order before you authorize
plainEnglish: An RO is a contract. Every line is a part, a labor hour, or a shop supply. If a line does not have a noun you understand, it is not authorized. Photograph the car and the part they say is bad. Grease-pencil the padded lines — that is what /quote is for.
safetyNotes: Do not sign “not to exceed” for a number you cannot pay.
Shop supplies and hazardous waste are fine as small fees. A $90 fuel-system cleaner is a product, not a fee.
steps: Read every line out loud. Part number, quantity, labor hours.
Circle anything named “service,” “package,” or “treatment.” Ask what broke.
Ask which lines are required for the complaint vs suggested.
Photograph the estimate. If they change it, you have the first page.
Authorize by line, not by total. Bring the RO to /quote if the numbers feel padded.

youtube.title: How to Avoid Getting Ripped Off by a Mechanic
youtube.whyThisVideo: Scotty on marking parts and refusing menu services — the RO literacy a first owner needs.

shopSentence: Please itemize parts and labor. I authorize [these lines] only. I want to see the old part.
askAtTheShop: Ask for the complaint in their words at the top of the RO. If it does not match what you said, stop.

title: EV owner: there is no oil change — here is what still wears
plainEnglish: A battery-electric car has no engine oil, no spark plugs, and no trans drain in the gasoline sense. You still have a 12-volt battery, tires, brake fluid, cabin filter, and coolant for the battery/inverter loop. Shops that quote an oil change on a Tesla are reading the wrong menu.
safetyNotes: Orange cables are high voltage. Do not open those covers.
Brake fluid and cabin filters are still real.
steps: Open the maintenance chapter. Circle: cabin filter, brake fluid, coolant (battery loop), tires, 12V battery.
Cross out engine oil, spark plugs, and exhaust. Those are not your car.
Regenerative braking means pads can last a long time — they still need a thickness check because they rust from not being used.
If a shop quotes oil, timing belt, or spark plugs, you are in the wrong stall.

youtube.title: Hybrid and EV Regenerative Braking Systems
youtube.whyThisVideo: Weber State (WeberAuto) explains regen so you understand why EV pads last — and why they still rust if you never use the friction brakes.

shopSentence: This is an EV. I do not need engine oil. Please follow the EV maintenance schedule: 12V, tires, cabin filter, brake fluid, and the battery-loop coolant.
askAtTheShop: Ask them to pull the EV service menu, not the gas menu for the same body style.

title: EV 12-volt battery: the little one that bricks the car
plainEnglish: The big pack moves the car. The little 12-volt battery wakes the computers, locks, and contactors. When it dies, a “full” EV will not unlock or charge. You jump the 12V posts in the manual — never the orange cables. Replacement is a normal battery job in a weird location.
partsNeeded: Correct 12V (some EVs are AGM or lithium 12V — match it)
safetyNotes: Do not cut orange high-voltage lines.
Use the labeled 12V jump points. Tesla and others hide them under a hood tab.
A dead 12V is not a dead traction pack.
steps: If the car is dark and the app is dead, think 12V first.
Open the manual to jump-start. Find the 12V posts. Jump like a gas car using those posts.
Once awake, get the 12V tested. EV 12V batteries often die younger than gas-car batteries.
Replace with the specified type. Recycle the old one.
If it dies again in weeks, the DC-DC converter (the thing that charges the 12V from the big pack) needs a tech — not another battery.

youtube.title: EVs Commonly Kill 12V Batteries! My Rivian Needed 2 New Ones
youtube.whyThisVideo: Out of Spec explains why EVs still have 12V, how the DC-DC charges it, and why these little batteries die early.

shopSentence: The EV will not wake. Please test and replace the 12-volt battery at the designated posts. Do not open the high-voltage pack for this symptom.
askAtTheShop: Ask 12V test results and whether the DC-DC is charging. Two 12V batteries in six months is a charging problem.

title: EV tires: weight, torque, and why they wear faster
plainEnglish: Electric cars are heavy and make instant torque. Tires work harder. Door-jamb PSI still wins. Some tires are marked for EV load and noise. A cheap low-load tire can wear 20% faster or feel vague. Rotate on schedule. This is the wear item oil used to be.
timeEstimate: 12 minutes to understand, 10 minutes to set PSI
partsNeeded: Tires that meet the load index on the sticker
safetyNotes: Do not drop load index to save money.
EV torque plus cheap tires is a wear and grip problem.
steps: Read the door sticker for size and PSI. EV PSI is often higher than you expect.
Check dates and tread. Rotate as the maker says — often more often than a light gas car.
When you replace, match load index and speed rating. Ask for EV-capable touring tires if the shop stocks them.
After install, set PSI and do the TPMS relearn the car wants.

youtube.title: Everything You Need To Know About Electric Car Tires
youtube.whyThisVideo: Jason Fenske (Engineering Explained) on weight, torque, noise, and why an EV tire is not “just a tire.”

shopSentence: Please set door-jamb PSI and confirm the load index on these tires matches the placard. I want an EV-capable tire, not the cheapest load-range they have.
askAtTheShop: Ask load index and whether the tire is rated for the vehicle weight. Alignment after uneven EV wear is a fair question.
